attempts.entry_title: Binocular selectivity of PV+ interneurons in mouse V1 (Scholl et al. 2015)
attempts.summary: In this data the paper's finding that PV+ interneurons in mouse V1 are more binocular and less disparity selective than PV- neurons mostly holds, with some values outside the paper's ranges, and so does the absence of a map for ocular dominance or disparity. Its central claim that PV+ cells match the ocular dominance and disparity preference of nearby neurons did not reproduce, on far fewer cells: 18 PV+ cells at the nearest radius against the paper's 86. The published files hold raw movies only, so the per-cell data came from an unpublished, undocumented folder covering part of the animals. The excitatory neuron comparison, histology and neuropil controls could not be tested, as those data are missing.
attempts.description: Attempts the findings of Scholl, Pattadkal, Dilly, Priebe and Zemelman (2015) on CRCNS pvc-10. The published folder holds raw two-photon movies and stimulus tables of six PV-Cre;Ai14 mice and no per-cell data; the per-cell structs of mice 7 to 10 in the bucket's undocumented folder original/to_remove/ are used to test 18 claims on 3 of the 6 animals, and 7 claims are blocked for data not deposited.

outcomes.notes: The post hoc anti-PV immunostaining (Experimental Procedures, Immunohistochemical Analysis) is not in the data set, whose published folder holds only two-photon movies, stimulus tables, plane shifts and 50 example masks. The paper names no other deposit.

outcomes.statement: Across 6 animals 338 PV+ neurons were identified, 115 (34%) visually responsive to monocular and 236 (70%) to binocular stimuli; of 3,982 PV- neurons, 944 (24%) were responsive to monocular and 2,001 (50%) to binocular stimuli.
outcomes.source: Results, Binocular Integration in PV+ and PV- cells of Mouse V1 Binocular Zone, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: we identified a total of 338 PV+ neurons, of which 115 (34%) were visually responsive for monocular stimuli and 236 (70%) were visually responsive for binocular stimuli. We identified 3,982 tdTomato ... (24%) were visually responsive for monocular stimuli and 2,001 (50%) were responsive for binocular stimuli
outcomes.notes: The counts are of all cells the paper identified by hand in 6 mice (338 PV+, 3,982 PV-) and of those responsive. The published folder (live/) holds no cell masks, labels or responses. The structs in original/to_remove/ hold only cells already selected: every PV+ cell in them passes the binocular index (58 of 58 in mice 8 to 10, 99 of 99 in mouse 7), and they cover mice 7 to 10 only, so the totals of identified cells cannot be counted. The binocmonocinds lists, which cover all 6 mice, total 109 PV+ and 769 PV- cells, against the paper's 115 and 944 monocular-responsive cells (data check); what they select is not documented. The dependent claims are tested on the responsive cells the structs and lists give: what blocks this claim is the missing record of the non-responsive identified cells, which those claims do not use.

We also observed a large fraction of PV+ cells with no evoked activity (28%) relative to nearby patches of active neuropil (Figure S3C).
outcomes.notes: The 28% is of PV+ cells with no evoked activity next to active neuropil patches. The structs hold one neuropil region per plane (neuropilpeaks identical for all cells of a plane), not the patches near each cell, and hold no non-responsive PV+ cells: every struct PV+ cell passes the binocular index (data check), so the fraction would be 0 by selection. The published folder holds neither. Figures S3A and S3B are single examples, not tested.

findings.statement: The published data set (pvc-10/live/) holds the raw green and red two-photon movies of 58 planes in 6 mice, their stimulus tables and plane shifts, and 50 unlabelled example cell masks for one plane (mouse5, depth 260). It holds no masks for the cells the paper analysed (identified by hand, 338 PV+ and 3,982 PV-), no PV+/PV- labels and no per-cell responses or positions. Processed per-cell data for part of the animals exist only in an unpublished folder of the bucket (next findings).

The data descriptor says the data set "contains information about the fluorescence traces, peak responses per condition, the measured binocular characteristics for each cell like its disparity selectivity index, preferred relative disparity, the position of the cell in the imaging volume". None of these per-cell data are among the published files; they are in pvc-10/original/to_remove/, which the file list and checksums do not include, for mice 7 to 10 only.

The bucket folder pvc-10/original/to_remove/, outside the data set's file list and checksums, holds MATLAB structs ce (PV-) and cePV (PV+), one entry per cell, with fields Ftrace, cyc, peaks, standard, dsi, disparitypref, peakfit, peakfitparams, masks, xy, xyshft, depth, sampleG, sampleR, neuropilcyc, neuropilpeaks, dsineuropil, date, filename and windowlength. They are made from the published movies: for 9 cells of mouse 8 at depth 205 um the stored Ftrace equals the mask mean of the published green movie in every frame, and for all 578 cells the trials per condition equal the stim file's repeats or one fewer. Readable structs cover mice 8, 9 and 10 (PV+ and PV-) and mouse 7 (PV+ only); the three mouse 7 PV- files (binoc7.mat, binoc7new.mat, 1452382802_binoc7.mat) are truncated and cannot be opened, and mice 5 and 6 have index lists only. Publishing complete structs for all six mice, with a description of their fields, would make the data set usable for the paper's analyses.

Nothing documents the structs or the binocmonocinds<mouse>[PV].mat index lists. The lists (109 PV+ and 769 PV- cells over 6 mice) look like the paper's visually responsive cells but cannot be confirmed. The field standard matches the responsiveness index of the Methods recomputed from peaks for 279 of 578 cells only; windowlength is 300 with no unit; neuropilpeaks is one region per plane; and the mouse 7 plane shift is stored in xyshft as (-70, 157) where stats.mat gives (157, -70) um.

The structs hold a selection of the paper's cells, not all identified cells: every PV+ cell in them passes the binocular responsiveness index (157 of 157), and 400 of 421 PV- cells of mice 8 to 10 do. Mice 8 to 10 hold 58 PV+ and 421 PV- cells against the paper's 338 PV+ and 3,982 PV- in 6 mice. The selection rule is not stated, so the paper's counts of identified cells cannot be checked.

The two rAAV CaMKIIa-nls-tdTomato mice of Figure 5, the neuropil patches of Supplementary Figures 3 and 5, and the anti-PV histology of Figure 1E are not in the data set (the structs hold one neuropil region per plane), and the descriptor does not say they were left out.
The descriptor gives frames of 255 by 456 pixels and converts positions with 300/456 and 300/255 um per pixel. Every frame in the files is 256 by 455 pixels, as the paper states.

The data set gives no frame rate. At the paper's 30 Hz, the median stimulus onset intervals give cycles of 3.93 s in mouse 5 and 4.37 to 4.43 s in mice 7 to 10, against the 4.5 s and 5 s that the stimulus durations in the stats files plus the Methods' 3 s blank give; only mouse 6 fits. Either the frame rate or the blank differs from the Methods in five of six mice.

Eight planes have fewer than the 6 to 7 repeats per condition the paper states (all six planes of mouse 10 have 4 or 5), and in four planes (mouse6 240 and 300, mouse8 250, mouse10 200) the last stimulus cycle runs past the last frame. Mouse 10 includes a plane at 125 um, above the 150 um the Methods give as the start. The structs hold the same numbers of trials per condition, so these planes were analysed with them.

verifications.reviewed: The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper's full text. The verifier read the bucket listing (keys and ETags), tested trial_dff and mask_traces on synthetic inputs, and had no attempt record. It found no place where the claims file misreads the paper (cell counts, neuropil wording, CaMKIIa passages). Its points, with the replies: (1) and (2) the folder original/to_remove/ was set aside because it "cannot be pinned", and the notebook said no per-cell measures exist, true of live/ only; the folder is now used for 18 claims, on the basis stated in the header and data check (public, under the data set's identifier, identified by ETag, made from the published movies), and the findings say the per-cell data are missing from the published folder and present, unpublished and partial, in original/to_remove/. (3) the struct date was not printed and an entry was not described; the notebook now prints one entry in full, the date per struct, mask sizes and centroids, and per-mouse counts. (4) the 0.5 s window was taken as 15 frames at 30 Hz while the onset intervals imply 26.2 to 26.6 frames/s; the clock check now shows the 13-frame window as well (2.60% against 2.59%), and the conflict stays a finding. (5) the window is placed on the average of all 50 masks, which is circular; the text now says so and a per-mask window is shown (2.83%). This cell decides no claim. (6) mouse 10 has 4 to 5 repeats and a plane at 125 um; the notebook now comments on both, and the structs hold the same trial counts. (7) the redundant conditional in cell 3 was removed.

Its points on text, with the replies: cell 18's printed sentence called the stored DSI the vector strength taken as measured while the same cell matches it with negatives set to zero for 578 of 578 cells; the print and the per-struct labels are corrected. The finding said trial counts match the stim files for all 578 cells where cell 18 checks the repeats or one fewer; corrected. The README and cell 0 said the stored traces equal the mask means of the published movies, shown for 9 cells on one plane; both now say so. The README said most outcomes rest on the cell set and are marked as assumed (the record marks 9 of 18, and fig3def's mark has no effect) and that counts are about half the paper's (18 of 86, 157 of 717, 130 of 1,090); both corrected, and fig3def is no longer marked. Its round-1 points B1 to B7 and C1 to C4 are resolved or kept as findings, as it accepted.

disagreements.reason: Judged on the L cell set alone. Under N, the attempt's version of the Methods' criterion, N with monocular cells, which is claims-file reading (b), puts all four values within tolerance with p = 0.0092. That is reproduced. The record reports both numbers but does not say why the main reading alone decides when the criteria say "under one reading". Reading (b) cannot be expressed under L at all, because L gives the same cells for joint and mono. Also, "0.4516 before rounding" appears in no output; cell 32 prints 0.452 (the outcome does not change, since 0.452 > 0.451).

Judged on the L cell set alone. Under N, mi-dsi-relation: N with joint cells meets the partial case (PV+ slope 0.059, PV- 0.151; cells 32, 45). The record needs to say why L alone decides. One round-1 reason is mis-pointed: for mi-dsi-relation the record writes "As for fig3abc"; the verifier's "Same as above" referred to fig3def's reason, that `dsi` is present for mice 8 to 10.

The criterion has no partial case. Two of its three conditions fail under every reading: 18 PV+ cells against 86 +/- 8.6, and the one-sided shuffle p is 0.015, against the required p < 0.01 (cell 56). By the criterion this is not reproduced. The record admits there is no partial case and assigns one anyway.

The partial case ("only the 50 um slope is significant") is met under claims-file reading 7b with axis 1b (cell 56): 50 um slope 1.42 +/- 1.94, p1 = 0.003, the largest slope; 75 to 150 um p1 from 0.478 to 0.996. Cell 58 and the record check only the full pattern ("No reading shown gives the pattern"). The partial case needs to be addressed. With an SE of 1.94, that 50 um value is fragile.

Partially reproduced, stated basis not supported. The partial case rests on the absence of significance under axis 1a, where the PV- slopes are unusable (6.70 +/- 6.19 up to 2.39 +/- 419.80). The Summary itself says 1b "gives slopes of the size the paper reports". Under main 1b, 100 um is significant (p1 = 0.002), so the absence fails (cell 61). The outcome could still stand on reading 3b with 1b: 50 um 0.09 +/- 0.04 (within tolerance), p1 = 0.013, and no other radius below 0.01. The record does not make that argument. Cell 62 and the record: "Under reading 1a, the absence at 75 to 150 um holds" rests on slopes with SEs up to 420.

Reproduced, rests on an unstated second choice. For unrestricted populations (a), 1a is the stable orientation, and no p2 falls below 0.10; that part holds. The record says restricted populations (b) also pass (p2 0.778 to 0.757), but those values come from 1a, where the SEs run from 4.29 to 308. In the stable orientation for (b), 1b, the main reading gives p2 = 0.036 at 100 um and 0.019 at 125 um (cell 64). So the outcome also rests on population reading (a). The record should state that as an assumption, as it does for figs6cd.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors. The Methods require responses above "neuropil activity (> 95% confidence interval)" without defining the neuropil region or the interval, and do not say how Fo and the 0.5 s window are placed for each trial. Read as the cell's mean above the plane neuropil's mean + 1.96 SE, the test keeps far fewer cells (41 PV+, 92 PV- passing the joint criterion where the binocmonocinds lists hold 81 and 189), and per-trial responses computed from the stored Ftrace with Fo the 10 frames before onset correlate with the stored peaks at r = 0.39 only. This attempt took the binocmonocinds lists as the paper's responsive cells. Which cells do those lists hold, and how were the neuropil test, Fo and the window computed?
